config.maid_self_talk.title: Maid Self-Talk
config.maid_self_talk.enabled.tooltip: Master switch. Maids will only talk to themselves / greet when enabled.
config.maid_self_talk.player_option_enab: Whether players can individually configure their maids (self-talk, inter-chat, custom prompt, tool calls). When off, the player options are greyed out; self-talk/inter-chat are treated as enabled, custom prompts are not injected and tool calls stay off.
When on, maid self-talk/inter-chat can actually invoke tools (switching work task, sitting, following, etc.). This changes game state and significantly increases token usage; off by default.
config.maid_self_talk.state_owner_online: Whether maids talk to themselves while their owner is online.
Minimum interval between self-talks in seconds.
Maximum interval between self-talks in seconds. The actual interval is random within this range.
Only trigger when there is a player within this radius (blocks).
How many self-talk records are kept in context. When exceeded, a forget happens and only the latest self-talk remains.
config.maid_self_talk.state_owner_offlin: Whether maids talk to themselves when their owner is offline but players are nearby.
Minimum interval between self-talks in seconds.
Maximum interval between self-talks in seconds. The actual interval is random within this range.
Only trigger when there is a player within this radius (blocks).
How many self-talk records are kept in context. When exceeded, a forget happens and only the latest self-talk remains.
config.maid_self_talk.welcome.enabled.to: Whether maids greet their owner after the owner logs in. Greetings are not limited by range: any maid in a loaded chunk can greet.
config.maid_self_talk.welcome.window_tic: Time window after the owner logs in during which maids may greet (20 ticks = 1 second).
config.maid_self_talk.inter_chat.enabled: Master switch for inter-maid chat. Maids will chat when a player is nearby and another maid is within maid range.
config.maid_self_talk.inter_chat.min_int: Minimum interval between inter-chat triggers in seconds.
config.maid_self_talk.inter_chat.max_int: Maximum interval between inter-chat triggers. Actual interval is random within this range.
config.maid_self_talk.inter_chat.player_: Only trigger when a player is within this radius (blocks).
config.maid_self_talk.inter_chat.maid_ra: Only trigger when another maid is within this radius (blocks) from the initiator.
config.maid_self_talk.inter_chat.keep_ro: How many rounds are kept in context. A Q/A counts as one round, single Q also counts as one. When exceeded, only the latest message remains.
config.maid_self_talk.inter_chat.chain_p: Probability (0~1) to continue the chain after each reply.
config.maid_self_talk.inter_chat.max_cha: Maximum messages produced by one inter-chat session (initiator's message included). The session ends when reached, guarding against extreme configs like chain probability 1.0.
config.maid_self_talk.event_context.enab: Master switch for environment awareness; when off, neither nearby events nor self-awareness are injected. When on, deaths and player hurts within a maid's perception radius are recorded, and together with the maid's own burning, drowning and injuries they are written up as natural-language background and injected into her next self-talk/inter-chat (not into greetings). Only players, owned animals and other maids are recorded for deaths; generic mob deaths are ignored. Death text is the vanilla localized message: English on a dedicated server, client language in singleplayer/LAN. These records live only in server memory and the current request; nothing is written to the world save.
config.maid_self_talk.event_context.rang: Perception radius in blocks for nearby deaths and player hurts. It does not constrain self-awareness: a maid's own burning, drowning and injuries are not distance-limited.
config.maid_self_talk.event_context.max_: Maximum buffered events per maid, shared by deaths, player hurts and self injuries; the oldest one is dropped when exceeded. The buffer is consumed and cleared on the next self-talk or inter-chat.
config.maid_self_talk.event_context.hurt: Whether player hurts are recorded. Only actual health loss counts (successfully blocked damage is not recorded). Hurt happens far more often than death, so this adds noticeable noise; off by default. To bound the backlog, one maid records player hurts at most once per second (fixed, not configurable), so the number of records is not the number of hits taken. Does not affect self-awareness.
config.maid_self_talk.event_context.self: Whether a maid senses her own state: burning, drowning, and her own injuries (including the damage source). Independent of the player hurt switch; turning player hurts off does not affect her own injuries. Self-awareness is not distance-limited and needs no player nearby; it only affects this maid's own next self-talk/inter-chat and is never shared with nearby maids.
config.maid_self_talk.event_context.hurt: How long a hurt record is kept, shared by player hurts and self injuries. Records older than this are dropped on the next record or dispatch and are no longer injected; records already dropped do not come back when the value is raised again. Death records have no lifetime. One maid records hurts at most once per second (fixed, not configurable), so only some hits in a burst are kept.
config.maid_self_talk.maid_identity.enab: Adds each nearby maid's UUID and current name to the nearby-entities context, so the model can tell same-named maids apart and recognize the same maid after a rename. How the name is resolved: a name tag wins; an unnamed maid using a built-in TLM model gets that model's preset name; an unnamed maid using a YSM or third-party custom model still counts as unnamed. Preset names follow the querying maid's chat language, falling back to English when that language has no translation. On by default; whether the item is registered is read once at startup, so restart after changing it. On a dedicated server, edit the server-side config.
config.maid_self_talk.maid_identity.tool: Registers the query_nearby_maids tool, which the model decides on its own whether to call: it returns every maid within a fixed 32 blocks with her UUID, current name and distance from the caller. Names resolve the same way: a name tag wins, an unnamed built-in model uses its preset name, an unnamed YSM or third-party custom model counts as unnamed, and preset names follow the caller's chat language. Independent of the injection above and can be toggled separately. On by default; whether it is registered is read once at startup, so restart after changing it.

Switching modes changes the request structure and may lower the prefix cache hit rate. Retrieval mode also sends extra requests; the real cost depends on model pricing, hit rate and recall length, so pick one and keep using it rather than switching often.
Retrieval is independent of the normal Tool toggle. In a continuous inter-chat, each maid plans only once, on her own first line.
